Module 4.title: Motivation Theories: Maslow & Herzberg
Module 4.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>Maslow's Need Hierarchy Pyramid</text><text x='80' y='75' fill='#ef4444' font-size='13'>Physiological → Safety → Social → Esteem → Self-Actualization</text></svg>
Module 4.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24HUT515 Module 4
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Herzberg Two-Factor Theory: Hygiene factors (salary, working conditions) prevent dissatisfaction; Motivators (recognition, responsibility) drive satisfaction.
  • McGregor's Theory X & Y: Theory X assumes employees dislike work; Theory Y views employees as self-motivated and creative.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Vroom's Expectancy Theory: Motivation = Expectancy × Instrumentality × Valence.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Money is a hygiene factor according to Herzberg; its absence creates dissatisfaction, but presence alone does not motivate.

Module 5.diagram_svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 500 130' style='width:100%;max-width:480px;height:auto;background:#0f172a;border-radius:8px;padding:10px;margin:10px auto;display:block;'><text x='20' y='25' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>Blake-Mouton Managerial Grid (9,9 Team Management)</text><text x='110' y='75' fill='#10b981' font-size='14'>High Concern for People + High Concern for Production</text></svg>
Module 5.short_notes:
⚡ High-Yield Exam Summary • 24HUT515 Module 5
📐 Core Governing Equations
  • Leadership Styles: Autocratic (directive), Democratic (participative), Laissez-faire (delegative).
  • Transformational Leadership: Inspires teams to transcend self-interest for visionary organisational goals.
📌 Essential Concepts & Rules
  • Collective Bargaining: Negotiation between trade unions and management on wages and working conditions.
  • Grievance Redressal: Formal multi-step escalation procedure for employee disputes.
💡 2-Minute Exam Revision Tips
  • Conflict resolution modes (Thomas-Kilmann): Competing, Accommodating, Avoiding, Compromising, Collaborating.
